rows.source: LT and frame factor are both unselected
rows.verdict: undefined — no adequacy test is possible

rows.source: the frame, hinge and stop build-up that turns a 900 mm leaf into a free width
rows.verdict: **a stated ytelse, and the free width is not demonstrated** — 40 mm is inside the range of ordinary frame and hinge build-ups and none is specified. If the build-up eats it this is a **deviation**, not a thin margin, and §2-2(1) allows one only by dispensation

rows.source: which of the three §11-13 readings applies
rows.verdict: **a stated ytelse, breached** — −500 mm on the strictest §11-13 reading. A shortfall against a stated number is a **deviation requiring dispensation** under PBL ch. 19, whose test is «klart større fordeler enn ulemper»; that is a stricter regime than a negative margin

rows.source: which of the three §11-13 readings applies
rows.verdict: **a stated ytelse, breached** — −500 mm on the sum rule. Same instrument as row 3: dispensation, not a margin. The two rows move together

rows.source: the timber fraction, which is width ÷ centres and not yet chosen
rows.verdict: **negative across the band** (−358 to −498) — sign robust, magnitude not

rows.source: the freeboard is a project choice, not a regulatory figure
rows.verdict: **a determination, not an analysis** — the freeboard is a project choice, so there is nothing to be adequate *to*. What §2-2(3) requires here is that the assumption be described and justified, and it is

rows.source: the stud fraction at a fixed insulation thickness
rows.verdict: **zero by construction** — the thickness was solved to hit 0.22 at 15 %, so the margin is zero there and the band across 8–23 % runs +0.0236 to −0.0274

rows.source: only one junction has been calculated, and the mean Ψ″ still rests on a generic range
rows.verdict: **negative across the band** (−0.0669 to −0.347) — sign robust, magnitude not

rows.source: no fraction is specified, so there is no limit to be short of
rows.verdict: **a determination, not an analysis** — no fraction is specified anywhere, so there is no limit to be short of. The duty is to describe and justify the assumption, not to state a margin against a number that does not exist

rows.source: the 100 mm reserve is a project allowance, not a measurement
rows.verdict: **a stated ytelse, met at exactly 4000 mm — zero by construction.** No margin was ever available to test: every option was solved *to* the envelope. Under the chapter 2 introduction a numeric level is **absolute** unless a tolerance is granted, so this is a design that spent an allowance that does not exist

rows.source: ground level, which no survey has fixed
rows.verdict: **sign set by the site** — +940 mm on the sewer route, −160 mm on the shallow tank

rows.source: C-07: the equipment masses and positions
rows.verdict: undefined — no adequacy test is possible

rows.source: the 1D requirement was computed on a surface that stops governing once any break is built
rows.verdict: **sign inverted by 2D** — the 1D requirement of 0.358 m²K/W was computed on the steel, which stops governing at the first millimetre of pad; the corner needs 0.80, so the margin is −0.80 as drawn, not +0.051

rows.source: both the flue's draught and the pressure a fan holds are assumption ranges
rows.verdict: **negative across the band** (−85.5 to −130) — and the only negative row whose resolution is not a number: a room-sealed stove removes the coupling instead of shrinking it, so the row is **retired** rather than made positive

rows.source: the soil's exhalation rate, which no site has measured
rows.verdict: **undefined** — the exhalation rate is a site input, so the sign is a site fact: the bound is +164 Bq/m³ on ordinary ground and −16 on alum shale, which is C-01's question and not the model's
